steps.instruction: Import the built-in Python modules and functions that will be used throughout this lesson. Start by importing the 'sys' module to access Python's system-specific parameters and functions.
steps.hint: Use the 'import' statement followed by the module name. This gives you access to Python's built-in data model components.

steps.hint: In Python, you define a function using the 'def' keyword followed by the function name and parentheses.
steps.analogousExample:

def greet():
    print("Hello!")
    # Function body goes here

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the main function. This will be the central place where we'll demonstrate Python's data model concepts.

steps.title: Create helper functions to demonstrate type checking
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, define a helper function named 'show_type' that takes one parameter and prints its type using the built-in type() function.
steps.hint: Use 'def show_type(value):' to define the function, then use 'print(type(value))' inside it.
steps.seedCode:
# Import the necessary built-in Python modules and functions here

# Your code will go below
def main():
    # Data model demonstrations will go here
    # Create integer and float variables here
    pass
    
    # Define helper function here
    def show_type(value):
        print(type(value))
steps.expectedOutcome: A helper function 'show_type' is defined inside main() that can display the type of any value passed to it.
successCriteria: The 'show_type' function is defined with one parameter and contains a print statement showing the type of that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a helper function to demonstrate Python's dynamic typing system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function prints the type using type() and print().
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a function named 'show_type' with one parameter and used print(type(value)) inside.

steps.hint: Use the show_type function you created earlier by calling it with each variable name as an argument. Place these calls after your variable initializations but before the end of the main function.
steps.analogousExample:

show_type(my_variable)
show_type(another_variable)
